title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover ordering
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: urgent customer impact observed during cross-region incidents where the SLO enforcer would trigger a regional failover too aggressively. Root cause: race between the in-memory backoff counter reset and the async health update path that marks nodes as unavailable; under load this produced transient ordering where all healthy nodes were marked unavailable, causing unnecessary failovers and repeated load-shedding. This hotfix stabilizes ordering in the enforcer coordinator, adds hysteresis to backoff transitions, and tightens the smoothing window for threshold changes.

What I changed: - Ensure health-update callbacks are processed before applying backoff resets (synchronized ordering at coordinator boundary). - Add hysteresis and minimum-stable-window to backoff->failover transitions to avoid thrashing on short spikes. - Emit new metric slo_enforcer.backoff_transition{from,to,region} for observability and alerting. - Fix a race in regional failover logic where the last-available-node check could be evaluated before the KV cache update completed. - Add unit tests for coordinator ordering and an integration test that replays the incident trace. - Add conservative default config and a runtime flag for gradual rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Reproduced issue in local canary harness and added regression test. - [x] Unit + integration tests added. - [x] CI green after flake fixes. - [x] Added release note and monitoring dashboards for new metric. - [x] Documented runtime flag and rollout plan in PR description.

Impact: This change reduces spurious regional failovers and excessive load-shedding during high churn periods. Defaults are conservative; we will roll out to a small subset of regions for 24h observation before global rollout.

Notes: This was filed as an on-call hotfix after an incident (SUP-4123). Engineering and SRE both validated the fix in staging and on a single-region canary prior to merge.
